theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.1
assumptions: d=1; I(λ)=∫exp(iλφ(x))ψ(x)dx, λ>0; smooth compactly supported amplitude suppψ⊂B1.
Part (1): p∈[1,∞), φ‴∈Lp(B1), ψ and ψ′ bounded; constants independent of φ,ψ,λ in this normalized class.
Part (2): derivatives through φ order4 and ψ order2 bounded via the displayed S norms.
proof_steps: Use y=sgn(x)sqrt(2φ(x)); retain u(y)=ψ(x(y))x_y(y) and u(0)=ψ(0)/sqrt(φ″(0)).
Fourier convention (2π)^(-1/2), Parseval and the quadratic oscillatory Fourier kernel isolate u(0).
Bound the remainder kernel in the dual Lp′ norm, or its second derivative version for λ^(-3/2).
theorem_cards.checked_derivation: PDF p3/p5 statement and normalization visually checked. The change-of-variable factor at 0 and remainder-power arithmetic were independently checked; external Fourier/oscillatory integral identities remain inputs.
gaps: Global fixed derivative bounds and support are indispensable to uniformity; this is a normalized class, not a constant uniform over arbitrary phases.
p=∞ is discussed in a remark but excluded from the stated p∈[1,∞); do not silently append that endpoint.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.2 decay only
theorem_cards.statement: Author remainder bound: |R(λ)|≲λ^(−1/(k+1)−1/((k+1)p′))(||φ^(k+2)||p||ψ||∞+||ψ′||∞). The Airy-type leading constant is not enabled as an exact callable formula in this card.
proof_steps: Normalize the phase to y^(k+1) by y=α_k(x)^(1/(k+1))x; track c_k=α_k(0)^(-1/(k+1))φ^(k+1)(0)^(1/(k+1)).
Use the inverse Fourier kernel Ai_k and its increment estimate to control the remainder by Hölder.
theorem_cards.author_claim: Author remainder bound: |R(λ)|≲λ^(−1/(k+1)−1/((k+1)p′))(||φ^(k+2)||p||ψ||∞+||ψ′||∞). The Airy-type leading constant is not enabled as an exact callable formula in this card.
theorem_cards.checked_derivation: PDF p5 and p6 original images checked. Exact remainder powers and normalized hypotheses retained as author claim; monomial Jacobian and Fourier factor discrepancy independently computed, leading formula quarantined.
gaps: PDF p5 theorem main term omits sqrt(2π) present in p6 proof. Eq(2.11) printed c_k also disagrees with monomial Jacobian: Pk=(1−t)^k/k!, so actual x_y(0)=((k+1)!)^(1/(k+1))/φ^(k+1)(0)^(1/(k+1)); printed c_k=(k+1)(k!)^(1/(k+1)). Both exact leading formulas are quarantined pending independent review.
Cannot use p=1 or p>2 through this theorem.

For x<0 and k+1 even, PDF p6 Eq(2.10) lacks the sign in the signed inverse derivative; the absolute-value comparability can survive. Use y=alpha_k(x)^(1/(k+1))x with its explicit branch; do not read an unsigned power of phi as the signed inverse derivative.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 2.6 printed main term
assumptions: d≥2; ψ supported in B_(1/1000); φ defined on B1 with φ(0)=0 and ∇φ(0)=0; A=Hφ(0).
Nondegenerate Hessian; S2(φ)≤C2 and |det Hφ|/S3(φ)≥C3>0 on stated domain.
theorem_cards.statement: The complete printed Th2.6 asymptotic (its main term together with the lower-order remainder R defined by that main term) is quarantined. The missing 2^(d/2) produces a leading-order residual, so the printed low-order R bound cannot be retained independently.
proof_steps: Quantitative Morse change φ(γ(y))=yᵀAy is asserted; transform amplitude to u(y)=ψ(γ(y))|det Dγ(y)|.
At y=0, the chain rule forces Dγ(0)ᵀ A Dγ(0)=2A, hence |det Dγ(0)|=2^(d/2).
The proof then substitutes ψ(0) for u(0), losing 2^(d/2). For φ(x)=|x|²/2, A=I and γ(y)=sqrt(2)y exhibit the discrepancy directly.
theorem_cards.author_claim: Printed main term has π^(d/2)λ^(−d/2)|det A|^(−1/2)ψ(0) times the displayed oscillatory phase. This printed exact normalization is quarantined and must not be cited as an accepted formula.
theorem_cards.checked_derivation: Independent determinant recomputation and a finite-S3 d=2 product model establish the missing factor within the source dimension domain d≥2. PDF p9–p10 confirm the print; each true 1D factor uses the separately checked Th2.1. The earlier d=1 illustration has been withdrawn as outside Th2.6; it is not a source-domain counterexample.
gaps: The exact main term omits the Morse Jacobian factor 2^(d/2).
Full quantitative Morse lemma and all remainder constants have not been independently proved; no repaired general remainder certificate is claimed.

A within-theorem d=2 model is φ(x1,x2)=(x1²+x2²)/2+x1³/100 and ψ(x1,x2)=η(x1)η(x2), where η is smooth, equals 1 near0, and is supported in (−1/2000,1/2000), so suppψ⊂B_(1/1000). On B1, Hφ=diag(1+0.06x1,1), Hφ(0)=I, S3=0.06, S2≤1.06, |detHφ(0)|/S3=50/3>0, and every displayed Sk bound through k=5 is finite uniformly in this fixed model. The oscillatory integral factors into two one-dimensional integrals to which the separately correct Th2.1 applies (e.g. p=2), giving 2π i λ^(−1)+O(λ^(−5/4)); the printed Th2.6 main term is π i λ^(−1) and its d=2 remainder bound is O(λ^(−3/2)). Thus the printed R=I−printed_main has nonzero λ^(−1) leading residual and cannot obey that lower-order bound. This uses Th2.1 separately in each coordinate and never uses Th2.6 to prove its own contradiction. No repaired general remainder certificate is claimed.

theorem_cards.label: Section 3 dispersive split
assumptions: The displayed source Example1 uses h(r)=sqrt(r+r³), r>0, with simple radial h″ zero r0=sqrt(2/sqrt(3)−1).
d≥2 for the stated polar/Bessel route; radial smooth cutoff on a fixed compact annulus away from r=0; derivatives and tangential factor h′(r)/r remain bounded and nonzero there.
|t| sufficiently large, |x|≥c|t| for a fixed c>0 as assumed in source p14; other spacetime region requires its own nonstationary argument.
Split |r−r0|≤δ and its complement, 0<δ small. On each far interval |h″|≥cδ; use normalized one-dimensional derivative estimates and imported Bessel expansion/decay.
theorem_cards.statement: Conditional source-model method: |I|≲|t|^(−d/2)δ^(−1/2), |II|≲δ |t|^(−(d−1)/2); balancing δ=|t|^(−1/3) gives |t|^(−(d−1)/2−1/3) in the explicitly stated radial/spacetime regime.
proof_steps: Split the support near and away from the radial Hessian zero.
Use nondegenerate estimate outside and the annulus thickness times tangential decay inside.
Balance the two displayed powers; do not use a zero derivative lower bound across the full support.
theorem_cards.author_claim: Method example: far contribution ≲t^(−d/2)δ^(−1/2), near contribution ≲δ t^(−(d−1)/2); balancing δ=t^(−1/3) gives t^(−(d−1)/2−1/3).
theorem_cards.checked_derivation: Original PDF p14 viewed. Powers balance exactly; required |x|≥c|t| and imported Bessel/one-dimensional estimates are retained. Radial Hessian eigenvalues independently recomputed. No arbitrary-phase or complete dispersive estimate is independently certified.
gaps: This is the source radial model; no arbitrary-phase or private half-density theorem follows.
The high-dimensional exact leading term is quarantined separately; only the split mechanism and power balancing are used.

Source p14 exact determinant display after(3.11) drops the tangential factor: radial Hessian eigenvalues are h″ and h′/r with multiplicity d−1, so detHω=h″(h′/r)^(d−1). Only comparability on an annulus with nonzero bounded tangential factor is available; the printed exact determinant is not used.

reusable_methods: Normalize support and finite derivative bounds before claiming a parameter-uniform constant.
Split stationary/degenerate regions before applying derivative bounds; retain the full Jacobian.
Balance geometric thickness and oscillatory decay only after both regions have valid estimates.
constant_dependence: Normalized 1D constants do not depend on φ,ψ,λ within stated hypotheses; high-dimensional constants depend on d,C2,C3,C4 and derivative norms. Exact high-dimensional main-term normalization is quarantined. The annulus example constants also depend on d, fixed cutoff/annulus, spacetime comparison c, phase derivative and Bessel bounds; its printed exact determinant has a separate missing tangential factor.
endpoint_limits: Derivative bounds hold on the whole active interval/region; p and k endpoints are stated separately.
